content: To search for a specific article on WikiDoc, you should type the desired word or topic into the search box located on the left-hand side of the screen and then press the Search button. Additionally, there is a Go button next to the Search button. The Go button only displays pages with titles that exactly match the term you entered. This makes the Go function a more restrictive search option, listing only pages with the exact name you input. If you know the precise name of the page you are looking for, the Go button allows you to navigate directly to that page without needing to follow links. Another way to search is by using categories. You can click on a category, such as Pulmonary or Nephrology, from the main homepage, and you will be presented with a list of all articles filed under that specific category. To view a complete list of all categories, you can click on Special:Categories. If you want to see a list of all pages in WikiDoc, you can either type Special:Allpages into the search menu or click on the Contents button located above and to the left. Searching Tips 1. Avoid short and common words: Including common stop words like the, one, your, more, right, while, when, who, which, such, every, about, or onto in your search terms will likely result in a failed search with no results. Short numbers and words that appear in half of all pages will also not be found. In such cases, remove these words and rerun the search. For more information, refer to Help: Common words, which explains how the database filters out stop words. However, you can still navigate to a page with a stop word in its title. Be aware that searching for combinations of words with the common word not may result in a database query syntax error due to a software bug. 2. Search is case-insensitive: Searches for acute MI, Acute MI, and ACUTE MI will all return the same results. 3. Do not use phrases: WikiDoc does not support searching for exact phrases. Enclosing a phrase in double quotation marks, such as can of tuna, will retrieve all pages containing the words can, of, and tuna, but not necessarily in that order or as a phrase. 4. Do not use regular expressions or wildcards: Regular expressions or wildcards (e.g., ) cannot be used in searches. If you are unfamiliar with these terms, you do not need to worry about them. To search for pages containing boat or boats, you should type boat or boats instead. 5. Do not search for words in single quotes: If a word appears in a page with single quotes, you can only find it by searching for the word with the quotes included. Since this is rarely desirable, it is better to use double quotes in pages, as this issue does not arise with them. An apostrophe is treated the same as a single quote. For example, Mu'ammar can only be found by searching for that exact term. However, a word with an apostrophe followed by s (e.g., doctor's) can also be found by searching for the word without the apostrophe and s (e.g., doctor). 6. Do not use the underscore character (_) as a space: The underscore character is not equivalent to a space. Using it in the URL will result in a search for a word containing actual underscores in those positions. 7. Be patient: There may be a delay in updating the search index. For reasons of efficiency and priority, very recent changes to pages may not be immediately reflected in search results. Search Options 1. How to browse filenames of images: To search for image titles, use Special:Imagelist. 2. Wiki text is searched: The search function looks through the wiki text (source text visible in the edit box). This distinction is important for piped links, interlanguage links, special characters (e.g., if ê is coded as ê, it will be found by searching for ecirc), and other similar cases. 3. Highlighting: Portions of matching pages that contain the searched terms are displayed, with the terms highlighted in red. You can adjust the number of lines extracted and the amount of text shown per line in your preferences. For example, searching for book will only return pages with that exact word, not pages with books alone. However, on pages containing both book and books, the book portion of the word books will also be highlighted.
